paras: Bougainville's scaly-toed gecko (Lepidodactylus mutahi) is a species of lizard in the family Gekkonidae. The species is endemic to Bougainville Island.
The specific name, mutahi, refers to the Mutahi area in northeastern Bougainville Island.

Adults of Lepidodactylus mutahi have a snout-to-vent length (SVL) of 3.7–5.6 centimetres (1.5–2.2 in). Adult males have a continuous series of 29–34 femoral/preanal/femoral pores extending almost from knee to knee.
The natural habitat of Lepidodactylus mutahi is forest, but it has also been found in artificial habitats such as gardens and banana plantations.
